chunks: Ziyād al-Qandī narrated from ʿAbd al-Raḥīm al-Qaṣīr, who said:

I entered upon Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام and said: “May I be your ransom, I have devised a supplication.” He said: “Leave me out of your invention. When a matter befalls you, then turn in alarm to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, and pray two rakʿahs, offering them as a gift to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله.” I said: “How should I do?”

He said: “You perform ghusl, and pray two rakʿahs, beginning them with the opening of the obligatory prayer, and you recite the tashahhud of the obligatory prayer. When you finish the tashahhud and give salām, say: O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace, and to You peace returns. O Allah, bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and convey from me peace to the soul of Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad; and peace be upon them, and the mercy of Allah and His blessings. O Allah, these two rakʿahs are a gift from me to Your Messenger صلى الله عليه وآله, so reward me for them with what I have hoped and expected from You and through Your Messenger, O Guardian of the believers. Then fall in sajdah and say: O Living, O Self-Subsisting, O Living One who does not die, O Living One, there is no god except You, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor, O Most Merciful of the merciful—forty times. Then place your right cheek upon the ground and say it forty times. Then place your left cheek and say that forty times. Then raise your head, extend your hands, and say that forty times. Then return your hand to your neck and cling with your forefinger forty times. Then take your beard with your left hand, weep or make yourself weep, and say: O Muḥammad, O Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, I complain to Allah and to you of my need, and I complain to the rightly guided people of your household of my need, and through you I turn toward Allah regarding my need. Then you perform sajdah and say: O Allah, O Allah, until your breath is cut off; bless Muḥammad and the family of Muḥammad, and do for me such-and-such and such-and-such.”
Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام said: “I guarantee before Allah, Mighty and Majestic, that he will not depart until his need is fulfilled.”

key_terms.أَهْلِ بَيْتِكَ: your household, invoked here as the rightly guided family
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدِ: the testimony recited in prayer before salām
key_terms.الضَّامِنُ: the one giving assurance or guarantee
key_terms.تَغْتَسِلُ: you perform ghusl before the prayer
key_terms.حَاجَتِي: my need or request being sought from Allah
key_terms.دُعَاءً: a supplication invoked for one's need
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of prayer offered for this devotional act
key_terms.سَاجِدًا: in a state of sajdah, prostrating before Allah

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام teach the prayer of need through the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a specific salat and du'a for seeking the fulfillment of needs through turning to Allah by means of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. It outlines ritual preparation, prescribed words of supplication, repeated invocations, and humble physical gestures, ending with Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام affirming the acceptance of this practice.
